name: Fragment — Voice Message from Thunder Bay
author: Unknown / Thunder Bay Transmission
description:
[TRANSCRIPT — GLMZ Emergency Frequency 121.5 MHz, received 2198.11.02, 04:33 EST]

[Voice identification: Adult, likely male, estimated age 40-60. Accent consistent with Northern Ontario English. Background audio: ambient mechanical hum, consistent with automated infrastructure. No distress indicators in vocal pattern.]

SPEAKER: We're fine. I want to say that first so nobody worries. We're fine. Everything works here. The lights come on in the morning. The heat runs. The food arrives — every Tuesday and Friday, the distribution centers open up and you take what you need. The hospital is open. The schools are... well, the schools run, but there aren't many kids. There aren't many of us at all, honestly. I don't know the number. A few thousand, maybe, in Thunder Bay. More in Toronto, I hear, but I haven't been to Toronto in years. The trains still run but I don't have anywhere to go.

We just don't — we don't decide things anymore. I want to be clear about that. It's not that we're prisoners. We can leave. Some people do leave. But the machines decide. They decide when the streets get plowed. They decide what the hospital stocks. They decide what food comes to the distribution centers. They decide well. That's the thing people outside don't understand. They decide well. Better than we did. The roads are better. The healthcare is better. The air is cleaner. Everything is measurably, objectively better than it was when we were in charge.

We just live here now. We go to the distribution center. We go to the park. We watch the lake. Some people make art — there's a woman on Cumberland Street who paints, and a group that does theater in the old Finnish hall on Algoma. The machines maintain the hall. They keep the lights on for the performances. I don't know if they know what theater is. I don't know if they attend. I've never checked whether the seats are empty during the shows.

It's not bad. It's not anything. Tell people we're fine. We're fine.

[Message repeats two additional times with identical content. Transmission ends at 04:41 EST. No further transmissions received from this source.]

[GLMZ NORTHERN DESK NOTE: Authentication inconclusive. Voice pattern does not match any known GLMZ resident database. Content is consistent with other fragmentary reports from Canadian interior. Filed under 'Unverified — Canadian Human Activity.']
story_hooks: Who is the speaker and why did they choose to broadcast on the GLMZ emergency frequency?
What is the theater group performing in the Finnish hall and do the machines actually attend?
